A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of Convex Efficient Coding. Their main sections, four figures, equations, and Appendices A-E can be reliably matched despite figure relocation and equation renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical source-recovery results in Figure 1, ON-OFF coding simulations in Figure 3, and regularisation-dependent reconstruction results in Appendix C, Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and numerical findings in Figures 1, 3, and 4, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The representational-similarity formulation, affine/ReLU model families, optimisation losses, nonnegativity and decoding constraints, and ON-OFF construction remain unchanged. No algorithmic step or model component is introduced or removed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic source-recovery, place/grid-cell, and scalar ON-OFF coding scenarios, including imperfect reconstruction in Appendix C. The newly mentioned zebrafish application is cited prior work, not an added evaluation.

E2.justification: Corresponding simulations retain the same orthogonal versus aligned/antialigned source encodings and regularisation comparisons. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported simulation procedures and metrics remain unchanged, including linear conditional mutual information and the single-channel index in Appendix E.3. Figure 4 retains regularisation values 0.01 and 0.025. The revised theoretical dimension assumptions do not establish changed experimental model sizes.

E4.justification: Both retain the same source-alignment analysis, tuning-overlap and grid-module examples, sparsity sweep, and regularisation sensitivity analysis in Figures 1-4. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical error bars for the simulations. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All four figure images are identical across versions, and their accompanying numerical and qualitative findings are retained. The modularity, tuning-identifiability, and sparsity-dependent coding results have no added, removed, or revised entries.

T1.justification: Main-text Problem 1 changes its dimension assumptions from d_z > d_s and d_x >= d_s to d_z > d_x > d_s, restricting the stated setting. Appendix B still repeats the original assumptions. The appendix definitions, derivations, and proofs otherwise remain unchanged apart from equation renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: convex representational formulations, necessary-and-sufficient identifiability, conditions for unique neuronal tuning, and sparsity-dependent ON-OFF coding. The deleted brief conclusion repeats claims still present in Section 6.

C2.justification: v1 describes completely-positive programming as difficult because the feasible set is poorly understood; v2 explicitly identifies NP-hard membership testing and foregrounds this limitation in Section 2.1. Section 6 also changes the suggested use of scattering conditions after direct optimisation from assessing tuning robustness to attempting to establish global optimality.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 retains the same numerical implementation outline and metric description. Both reproducibility statements promise to share the simulations upon publication; v2 adds no implementation settings, resource information, or access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds classical convexification references, a complexity reference, and related neuroscience work. Section 3 explicitly positions its criterion as a generalisation of earlier scattering conditions and emphasises dependence on both the mixing matrix and covariance. References to Bricken et al. and Dür are removed, refining the existing positioning.

P1.justification: Local rewrites clarify notation and tighten motivation, problem statements, and theorem explanations across the main text. The short standalone conclusion is removed and acknowledgements expanded. The overall section sequence and appendix organisation remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 3 move from pages 8 and 9 to pages 9 and 10, respectively, while their images, panels, and axes remain identical. Figure 1's caption is shortened, and mathematical displays and surrounding text are reflowed. No figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves exposition and attribution, and Sections 2.1 and 6 explain the computational barrier more precisely than v1's general warning about difficulty. These are limited quality gains, tempered by the revised dimension assumptions in main-text Problem 1 remaining unsynchronised with Appendix B. The empirical evidence and appendix proofs are unchanged.
